title: Why is English spelling so strange?
examples: Why are there silent letters in English?
Why is English spelling so hard?
What was the Great Vowel Shift?

explain.say: Here is a puzzle: why does knight have a k you cannot hear? Look at the board. Long ago, people really said every part: k, n, then a throaty sound for g, h, then t. Kuh-nicht! The first box, k, was spoken.

draw.text: Why is English spelling so strange?

explain.say: See the third box, igh? It once made a scratchy sound, like the ch in Scottish loch. Over hundreds of years people stopped saying it. But the spelling stayed frozen. So silent letters are fossils of old sounds! Can you think of another silent letter?
Now look at the timeline on the board. After 1066, French-speaking scribes, people who wrote things down for a living, spelled English the French way. That is why queen has qu, from French.

explain.say: Next, look at the vowel shift, from about 1400 to 1700. The long vowels slowly moved: bite was said like beet, and house like hoose. But see the printing stop, 1476? Printing froze spellings before the sounds finished changing.

explain.say: You are a spelling historian! Look at the last stop: in 1828 Noah Webster changed American spellings, like colour to color. Wow: English spelling is a museum of its own history. Challenge: find the silent letter in island, then look up why it is there!

faq.q: Why are there silent letters in English?
faq.a: Many silent letters were once spoken, like the k in knight and knee. People stopped saying them, but the spelling did not change.
asks: Why is the k in knife silent?

faq.q: What was the Great Vowel Shift?
faq.a: Between about 1400 and 1700, the long vowel sounds of English changed: bite was once said like beet, and house like hoose. Spelling mostly kept the old forms.
Printed books spread the same spellings across the country from 1476 on, so spelling settled while pronunciation kept changing.

faq.q: Why is island spelled with an s?
faq.a: Island comes from Old English iegland, with no s. Writers added the s in the 1500s because they wrongly linked it to the Latin-based word isle.

faq.q: Why do Americans spell colour as color?
faq.a: Noah Webster's 1828 dictionary simplified many spellings, like color, center and theater, and American English kept them.

facts: The s in island was added in the 1500s by mistake, after the unrelated word isle.
Noah Webster published An American Dictionary of the English Language in 1828.
